record.paper_title: Open Questions On Nuclear Collective Motion
record.context_brief: Extending tidal waves beyond yrast vibrational states
record.original_question: Can the tidal-wave approach, which treats yrast states of vibrator-like nuclei as semiclassical rotating mean-field states, be extended to describe rare enhanced E2 transitions parallel to the yrast sequence among off-yrast vibrational-multiplet states in shell-model spectra such as 62Ni?

evidence.quote: These are the yrast states of the vibrator multiplets described in a semiclassical way. This mode has been called ”Tidal Wave” (TW), because it has wave character: the energy and angular momentum increase with the wave amplitude while the frequency stays constant.

The Shell Model calculation shows enhanced transitions parallel to the yrast sequence, which correspond to the rare members of the vibrational multiplets. An extension of the tidal wave approach to describe these states seems promising.
The remaining part of the Shell Model transition pattern looks chaotic. The coherence of the vibrational motion is lost.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Consider an even–even near-spherical (vibrator-like) atomic nucleus described in a shell-model framework. Its low-lying collective states are organized into approximate quadrupole vibrational multiplets labeled by a phonon number N = 0, 1, 2, …, with each N-phonon multiplet containing several states of definite angular momentum I. The yrast line is the sequence of lowest-energy states for each spin I; for a harmonic vibrator the yrast member of the N-phonon multiplet has spin I = 2N.

The tidal-wave (TW) description treats the yrast vibrational states as a single semiclassical rotating mean-field configuration: a uniformly rotating quadrupole-deformed shape obtained from the self-consistent cranking model, in which angular momentum is generated by increasing the deformation amplitude at (approximately) constant rotational frequency, rather than by increasing the frequency at fixed deformation as in a rigid rotor. In this picture, the yrast E2 transitions B(E2; I → I−2) along the vibrational ground band are reproduced as the classical quadrupole radiation of the rotating mean-field shape.

Empirical/shell-model observation to be modeled. Large-scale shell-model calculations for vibrator-like nuclei (for instance, ⁶²Ni) reveal, in addition to the yrast sequence, a set of comparatively rare but enhanced E2 transitions running parallel to the yrast line: namely, transitions between off-yrast members of successive vibrational multiplets that connect the same non-yrast spin I in the N-phonon multiplet to spin I−2 (or the corresponding off-yrast state) in the (N−1)-phonon multiplet. The remaining off-yrast E2 strengths form a comparatively incoherent (chaotic-looking) background.

Problem. Construct an extension of the tidal-wave approach—still based on semiclassical, self-consistent rotating mean-field configurations (e.g., excited cranking solutions, additional collective or quasiparticle excitations built on top of the tidal wave, or analogous coherent semiclassical modes)—that:

(a) reproduces the yrast tidal-wave description as a special case;
(b) yields a discrete family of additional rotating configurations whose E2 decay pattern reproduces the enhanced off-yrast transitions parallel to the yrast sequence found in shell-model calculations of vibrator-like nuclei such as ⁶²Ni;
(c) explains, within this semiclassical mean-field picture, why the remaining off-yrast E2 strength appears incoherent; and
(d) gives quantitative predictions for excitation energies and B(E2) values of these off-yrast states that agree with the shell-model results.

Does such an extension exist, and if so, formulate it explicitly?
artifact.status_search_result: A literature search shows the tidal-wave approach has been formulated and applied to yrast states of near-spherical and transitional nuclei (e.g., ¹⁰²Pd, A≈100 region) and that shell-model studies of ⁶²Ni discuss collective and single-particle excitations, but no published work extending the tidal-wave/cranking semiclassical description to off-yrast vibrational-multiplet states with enhanced parallel E2 transitions was found. The proposed extension thus appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Tidal waves as yrast states in transitional nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Tidal wave generates angular momentum by increasing deformation at approximately constant frequency; describes yrast states of vibrator-like nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: TW approach is established for yrast states only.

status_evidence.title: Tidal Waves -- a non-adiabatic microscopic description of the yrast states in near-spherical nuclei
status_evidence.snippet: Microscopic cranking description of yrast states in near-spherical nuclei.
status_evidence.claim: Existing TW formulations target yrast states.

status_evidence.title: Single-particle and collective excitations in 62Ni
status_evidence.snippet: Shell-model and experimental study of yrast and off-yrast excitations in 62Ni.
status_evidence.claim: 62Ni exhibits non-trivial off-yrast structure relevant to the proposed extension, but no TW extension is presented.

status_evidence.title: Tidal wave in 102Pd: Rotating condensate of up to seven d-bosons
status_evidence.snippet: Applies TW to yrast states of 102Pd via rotating d-boson condensate.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent TW work continues to focus on yrast configurations.
